unit: One within-paper contrast of wall treatments, with the facts recorded from the source. Repetitions over grids, Reynolds numbers or stations of one flow case are one row.

rule.text:
# Fact rules for three evidence groups (version 2)

Written on 19 November 2026 after the second reading of 36 works and before any
reading made under these rules. Readers record facts with their source locations. A
script derives every membership and status from the facts. Readers do not type a
membership.

The question behind the three groups: which published tests can isolate the effect of
a wall treatment (A), which examine an assumption shared by a class of wall models
(B), and which test a fitted wall treatment outside the data that determined it (C)?

## Definitions

**Wall treatment.** What the source itself defines as its wall model, wall function
or near-wall treatment: the relation that supplies the wall stress, or wall-adjacent
turbulence quantities or boundary values, to a calculation that does not resolve the
viscous sublayer, together with the components the source assigns to it (for example
the sampling height, time filtering of its input, a modified eddy viscosity in the
first cell, or the way the stress is imposed). A calculation that applies the no-slip
condition on the same under-resolving grid has the treatment "none".

**Contrast.** Two or more calculations reported by the same source ("arms") for the
same flow case that differ in the wall treatment or in how one wall treatment is
implemented. A wall-resolved calculation on a finer grid, a DNS and an experiment are
references, not arms. Results taken from other publications are arms only if the
source states that they were obtained with the same solver, grid and settings.

**One row per contrast.** Repetitions of one contrast over several grids, Reynolds
numbers, stations or outer closures of one flow case form one row; name the
repetitions in `replicates`. Different flow cases and different kinds of variant
(`variant_type`) are different rows. Several treatments compared together on one case
form one row that lists all arms.

## A. Contrast facts

- `feedback`: one of
  - `coupled LES` (the treatment acts in a running scale-resolving simulation,
    including lattice-Boltzmann and other discretisations);
  - `coupled hybrid RANS-LES`;
  - `coupled RANS`;
  - `prescribed input` (the treatment is evaluated on reference or stored fields and
    its output is not fed back: a-priori and offline tests);
  - `other` (say what).
- `variant_type`: one of
  1. `different model`: the arms use different laws, closures, estimators or learned
     models as wall treatment; or one arm has no wall treatment on the same grid; or
     one arm imposes reference (exact) wall stress in the running calculation. A
     learned model retrained on different data or with a different architecture or
     input set is a different model.
  2. `same model, different imposition`: the output of one model is applied to the
     solver in different ways (for example a stress boundary condition against an
     effective wall viscosity; aligned against unaligned stress direction; an imposed
     near-wall profile of a turbulence quantity against none).
  3. `same model, different input`: one model receives its input differently on the
     same grid (sampling height or cell; time or space filtering of the input).
  4. `same model, different parameter`: one constant, coefficient or setting of one
     model form differs.
  5. `same model, different numerical solution`: the same model equations solved by a
     different numerical method or on a different internal model grid.
  6. `wall-cell discretisation`: the discretisation of the outer solver in
     wall-adjacent cells or particles changes; the wall model does not.
- `components_changed`: the components of the wall treatment that differ between the
  arms (for example "stress law", "first-cell eddy viscosity", "sampling height").
- `factors`: for each of `grid`, `outer_closure` (subgrid model, or the RANS closure
  away from the wall), `numerics` (solver, schemes, time step), `forcing` (driving
  pressure gradient or mass flow, inflow and the boundary conditions other than the
  wall), `reynolds_number` and `domain`, one of
  - `fixed`: the source states that it is the same in the arms, or the source
    describes one set-up for the compared runs and names no difference;
  - `varied`: the source states a difference between the arms. For a repeated
    contrast, judge within each compared pair, not across the repetitions;
  - `unreported`: the source does not describe this factor for one of the arms, or
    the arms come from separately described set-ups whose match is not stated.
  A component that the source assigns to the wall treatment is not a varied factor.
  It belongs in `components_changed`. An outer closure replaced throughout the flow
  together with the wall model is a varied `outer_closure`.
- `averaging`: `equal`, `different` or `unreported`, with the stated lengths. It is
  recorded and does not affect membership: the averaging window changes sampling
  precision, not the expected value.
- `reference_comparison`: one of
  - `tabulated`: numbers for every arm and for a reference, in a table or the text;
  - `plotted`: curves or symbols for every arm and for a reference on common axes;
  - `qualitative`: contours, visual impressions or statements, without values for the
    arms and a reference on a common scale;
  - `none`: the arms are compared only with each other.
  A reference is a DNS, a wall-resolved LES, an experiment, an analytic solution or a
  named correlation.
- `hydrodynamic_observables`: the velocity, stress, pressure, force or separation
  quantities for which that comparison is reported. `thermal_observables` are listed
  separately and do not make a member.
- `source_location`: section, table or figure numbers and PDF page numbers.

### Derived membership (script)

"Comparable" means: `feedback` is coupled LES, coupled hybrid RANS-LES or coupled
RANS; `reference_comparison` is tabulated or plotted; and there is at least one
hydrodynamic observable.

- **Strict**: comparable, `variant_type` = different model, all six factors `fixed`.
- **Broad**: comparable, `variant_type` is one of types 1 to 4, all six factors
  `fixed`. Every strict contrast is broad.
- **Upper bound**: comparable, types 1 to 4, no factor `varied`, at least one factor
  `unreported`.
- Otherwise the contrast is not a member, and the reason follows from the facts:
  prescribed input; a factor varied; no quantitative common reference; a
  numerical-solution or discretisation variant; thermal observables only.

A work is a strict, broad or upper-bound member if it has at least one such contrast.
The evidence group `controlled_wall_change` is the broad membership. The strict and
upper-bound counts are its reported sensitivity.

Each coupled LES, hybrid or RANS design receives a derived baseline label from its
contrasts, the first of the following that applies: broad member -> "identified
within-setting alternative"; upper bound only
-> "within-setting alternative with a control unreported"; a factor varied ->
"whole-system or multiple simultaneous changes"; no quantitative common reference ->
"alternative compared without a quantitative common reference"; only type 5 or 6, or
only a sweep of grid, Reynolds number or input with one treatment -> "same wall
treatment: grid, Reynolds number, numerical solution or discretisation varies"; one
treatment and no sweep -> "no distinct wall-treatment baseline identified". A design
without solver feedback receives "not applicable (not a coupled LES or RANS series)".

## B. Constitutive-constraint facts

A constitutive test examines an assumption shared by a *class* of wall models, using
reference data and without evaluating any wall model. Record a candidate whenever a
source examines such an assumption. Facts for each candidate:

- (i) `restriction`: the restriction on a class of wall mappings that the source
  names, with its location. Examples: the wall stress is a function of the
  instantaneous velocity at one sampling point; the wall stress is aligned with the
  velocity at the sampling height; convection and pressure gradient are negligible or
  balance in the modelled layer (equilibrium). A property of one model's fitted
  parameters is not a class restriction.
- (ii) `reference_only_paired_data`: true if the source reports data from a DNS, an
  experiment or a wall-resolved LES alone that pair the inputs of that class with the
  wall quantity (or that give the terms of the assumed balance), at a stated sampling
  height or filter; with location.
- (iii) `violation_statistic`: true if the source reports a statistic of those
  reference data, computed without evaluating a wall model, that could show the
  restriction violated: a joint or conditional distribution, a scatter, a correlation,
  time lag or angle between the paired quantities, or the size of the terms the class
  neglects; with location. The error of a model's prediction is not such a statistic.

A work is a member of `constitutive_constraint` if at least one candidate has (i),
(ii) and (iii) all true. The output of a particular model evaluated on reference
inputs is a prescribed-input test and not a member.

## C. Transfer facts

Record one row for each flow case in which a *fitted* wall treatment is evaluated at
a condition outside its fitting set.

- "Fitted": weights, coefficients or constants determined, by the source or by the
  cited work that supplies the frozen model, from data of named flows (training of a
  learned model, regression or optimisation of coefficients, tuning of a constant by
  numerical experiments). A classical law with textbook constants is not fitted
  unless the source re-tunes it. Held-out snapshots or realisations of a fitting flow
  at a fitting condition are inside the fitting set and give no transfer row.
- (a) `fitting_set`: the flows and conditions that determined the weights or
  coefficients (geometry, Reynolds number, pressure gradient; grid or sampling height
  where these are part of the data); with location.
- `target`: the tested flow case and condition, and the observables.
  `transfer_dimension`: what differs from the fitting set (Reynolds number; geometry;
  pressure gradient or regime; grid or sampling height; solver). `feedback` as in A.
- (b) `selection_decisions`: every documented choice among candidate models, inputs,
  architectures, hyperparameters, thresholds or settings. For each: what was chosen,
  the data used, `uses_target` (yes / no / not stated: whether those data include the
  target flow case at the target condition), and the location. An empty list if the
  source documents none.
- (c) `variants_compared_on_target`: true if the source reports results of two or
  more variants of the fitted treatment at the target condition.
- (d) `frozen_external`: true if the weights or coefficients were published earlier
  and are applied unchanged in a work that shares no author with the fitting work, as
  far as the printed author lists show.
- (e) `holdout_statement`: true if the source states explicitly that the target
  condition was used neither for training nor for validation or model selection (for
  example a table of training, validation and test cases that lists it as test
  only); with the passage. A statement about training alone is false here.

### Derived status (script)

- `partly exposed`: a selection decision has `uses_target` = yes, or (c) is true.
- otherwise `qualified`: (d) or (e) is true.
- otherwise `selection unresolved`.

Reported: the three counts of tests and of works, and the range of tests "not shown
to be exposed", from the qualified count to qualified plus selection unresolved.

## Scope

The facts describe what a source documents. An unreported control or an undocumented
selection history is a statement about the report. It does not show that the control
differed or that the target was used. Memberships are documentary: they say that a
comparison of a given design exists, not that the treatment was validated.

derived_by: Membership is computed from the recorded facts by the rule; no membership was typed by a reader.

records.case: Isothermal fully developed flow between parallel plates, Re_tau about 5200
arms: nutWallFunction: standard logarithmic wall function for nu_t (Eqs 8-11), panels a
nutWakeFunction: nu_t from Luchini's interpolated law of the wall plus wake function (Eqs 20-24, Tables 1-2), panels b
nutCfFunction: nu_t from a friction-factor correlation (Eq. 28 with the smooth-pipe friction factor Eq. 31, effective diameter D_eff = 2 D_h/3, mean velocity from Eq. 24), panels c
components_changed: law that sets the first-cell turbulent viscosity nu_t (and hence the wall shear stress): log law, law of the wall plus wake, friction-factor correlation
records.factor_notes: Grid: each treatment is run on the same three uniform meshes (5, 10, 20 cells per channel height; legends of Figs 1-2). Closure: Fig. 1 is entirely standard k-epsilon, Fig. 2 entirely realizable k-epsilon. Numerics: 'The solver buoyantFoam was used to conduct the complete set of simulations ... In all cases, steady-state simulations were conducted with second-order spatial discretization schemes' (Sec. 3, p. 6). Forcing and Reynolds number: 'the velocity inlet value was obtained iteratively in each case to guarantee that the correct Re_tau is achieved' (p. 8), so every arm is driven to the same Re_tau while the inlet velocity is tuned per run and not reported; recorded as fixed because the stated control quantity is identical (see uncertain_points). Domain: one two-dimensional channel set-up with length 'selected to ensure developed flow conditions at the outlet'; no difference named.
records.averaging_note: Steady-state RANS solutions; no time averaging involved (Sec. 3).

hydrodynamic_observables: mean streamwise velocity u+ versus y+
records.replicates: three meshes (5, 10, 20 cells per channel height) times two outer closures (standard k-epsilon, Fig. 1; realizable k-epsilon, Fig. 2)

Closure: 'Each turbulence model is tested with each wall treatment inside the same family' (pp. 2-3), so each pair shares its k-epsilon variant. Numerics: 'All simulations are performed using ANSYS Fluent ... The solution algorithm chosen for these simulations is SIMPLE' (p. 2). Forcing: one set of operating conditions (Table 2); 'the rest of the simulations are performed by using only fully developed velocity and pressure profiles' (p. 4), generated by the same recycling procedure in every run. Reynolds number: never stated; same inlet velocities and fluid in all runs. Domain: Table 1 gives the pipe length only as a range, 100-1,000 cm; the length used for Figs 3-4 is not stated, but one geometry is described and the correlation lines in Fig. 3 are the same for all runs.

records.reference: Correlations of Serth (2007) and Sinnott (2012) and the Colebrook friction factor with the Rothfus et al. (1950) correction (horizontal lines in Fig. 3); for U the correlations of Sinnott, Serth and Levenspiel (Fig. 4)
hydrodynamic_observables: inner-tube pressure drop
outer-tube (annulus) pressure drop
records.replicates: three outer closures: standard, RNG and realizable k-epsilon
records.note: Fig. 3 gives one symbol per run with the three correlation lines; relative errors are quoted in the text for some runs only (scalable with standard k-epsilon about 4.1% from Colebrook; Menter-Lechner with RNG 2.0% inner and 0.87% outer from Serth; scalable with realizable up to 16%). The source concludes that 'results show a major dependence on the wall treatment used that on the turbulence model itself' (p. 4). The three correlations differ among themselves by 8-24% in pressure drop. The first-cell y+ is not reported, so it is not known whether the selected mesh (12 inflation layers) resolves the viscous sublayer.

records.source_location: Secs 2.2.3 and 2.3.3, Figs 3, 4 and 5 (PDF pp. 4-7, 10)
records.case: 2DZP flat plate, M = 0.2, Re = 5e6, dx = 0.5e-3 (y+ ~ 90 at X = 0.97)
arms: initial method ('initial'): Spalding-law-type wall function (Knopp 2006) evaluated at the image point; wall stress imposed through a velocity embedded in the IB cell by tau_w = (mu + mu_t) du/dy (Eq. 1), the same embedded values used for inviscid and viscous fluxes; image-point velocity 0th-order extrapolated from the nearest cell; k Dirichlet (Eq. 5), epsilon Neumann (Eq. 6); Pk from one-sided strain between fluid and IB cells

modified method ('modified'): same wall function; wall-stress flux at fluid-IB interfaces converted into a body force on the adjacent fluid cell (Eq. 7); symmetric condition du/dy = 0 (Eq. 8) for the inviscid flux; image-point tangential velocity by least-squares linear reconstruction (Eq. 9); tau_w propagated into the fluid (Eq. 10) and two-layer (Chieng-Launder) wall-function production of k blended with the bulk production (Eqs 11-15); dk/dy = 0 at the wall; epsilon and the k-destruction term set algebraically by Eq. (13) where y0 < 2 dx
components_changed: way the wall shear stress is imposed (embedded ghost-cell velocity versus body force on the adjacent fluid cell)
IB-cell velocity used for the inviscid flux (wall-function-embedded velocity versus symmetric condition)
reconstruction of the image-point (sampling) velocity (0th-order extrapolation versus least-squares linear fit)
near-wall production term of k (strain-based versus log-law wall-function form, two-layer averaged and blended)
wall boundary condition of k (Dirichlet from tau_w versus dk/dy = 0)
near-wall epsilon (transport equation with Neumann condition versus algebraic value for y0 < 2 dx)
records.factor_notes: One set-up is described for both methods: Table 1 (p. 4) gives one list of schemes, standard k-epsilon and the Spalding-law-type wall function; dx = 0.5e-3 and M = 0.2, Re = 5e6 are stated once (Sec. 2.2.3 p. 4); 'The modified method was then evaluated by 2DZP as with the initial method' (Sec. 2.3 p. 6) and 'evaluated again using the 2DZP problem' (Sec. 2.3.3 p. 10). The near-wall changes to the k and epsilon equations and to the IB flux evaluation are assigned by the source to the IB/near-wall treatment ('imposition of boundary conditions on immersed boundaries; near-wall treatments of k-epsilon models', p. 2), so they are listed as components, not as varied factors. Fig. 8: drag 0.31 (k-omega high Re), 0.27 (k-epsilon high Re), 0.32 (k-omega low Re), 0.27 (k-epsilon low Re), measured 0.279; lift 0.091, 0.035, -0.027, -0.080, measured 0.004. Fig. 9 relative drag error: -11.34, 1.91, -14.09, 3.43 %. Figs. 10-12 (pressure, wake velocity, wall shear stress contours) compare the four runs with each other only. The 'low Re' runs resolve the near-wall layer (y+ 1-10) on a finer near-wall mesh; under the rule they could also be read as wall-resolved references, which would leave the two high-Re runs, differing in turbulence model, as the only arms. Sec. 2.2 (PDF p. 3) states the two methods the other way round ('low Reynolds number wall treatment ... uses wall functions ... high Reynolds number ... the viscous sublayer is resolved'); Abstract, Sec. 1, Sec. 4.2, Table 1 and Fig. 7 consistently assign y+ 30-300 to the high Re method and y+ below 10 to the low Re method.

# Settlement of the disagreements between the two readings: plan fixed before any third reading

Written on 19 November 2026 after the agreement statistics were computed
(`fresh/fresh_agreement.json`, `rare_group_agreement.json`, both of 11:07 UTC) and
before any settlement answer existed. The time of fixing and the SHA-256 values are in
`settlement_freeze.txt`. The decision rule of `protocol/agreement_plan_v2.md` is not
changed by this file. This file says how its condition (d) is carried out.

## What is settled

The item list is produced by `codes/stage_settlement.py` from the stored agreement
files. It is not chosen by hand. For every work read twice in this pass it lists:

1. **scope**: the two readings give a different disposition (eligible, contested,
   excluded);
2. **contrasts**: strict, broad or upper-bound membership differs;
3. **groups**: prescribed-input, coupled-LES, RANS or thermal membership differs and
   the difference does not follow from the disposition alone;
4. **constitutive**: derived constitutive membership differs;
5. **transfer**: the readings differ on whether the work has a fitted treatment or a
   transfer row, a matched row has a different derived status, or a row was found by
   one reading only (`work/transfer_row_matches.json`).

Two further questions go to the same third reading:

6. **verify**: for each work that is a broad or upper-bound member in the version-2
   first reading and was not read a second time in this pass, the facts of every
   member contrast are checked against the source. This covers the membership changes
   in `work/change_table.json` that no independent reading has confirmed.
7. **sublayer**: see "Scope boundary" below.

System-benchmark disagreements are not settled item by item. That label is one of the
five regression groups, it carries no decision under the plan, and its failure
(kappa 0.15) is examined as a change of instrument in `regression_diagnosis.json`.
No system-benchmark count is quoted whatever that examination finds.

## How a scope disagreement is decided

The disposition of a work is governed by the paper-level rule published with the
collection (`data/revision/eligibility_rules.json`, unchanged since it was written):

> Include a work in the evidence frame when a source-located comparison tests a named
> treatment, its imposed response, a stress estimator, or a whole calculation using an
> identifiable wall treatment. The paper needs one qualifying design. An application
> without such a comparison, a wall-resolved flow study with no tested wall treatment,
> and unavailable evidence do not enter by default.

The sentence in `rules_v2.md` that defines a wall treatment ("... to a calculation
that does not resolve the viscous sublayer ...") was written to identify the arms of a
contrast. The second reader was given both texts; the first reader was told to copy
the earlier disposition unless the source contradicted it. Where the two texts give
different dispositions for facts on which the readings agree, the disagreement is
attributed to **rule ambiguity**, not to either reading. Where a reading states a fact
that the source contradicts, it is attributed to that reading.

Three clarifications are fixed here, before the third reading, and are applied to
every work of the kind, not case by case:

- **S1, near-wall methods on a grid that reaches the viscous sublayer.** A hybrid
  RANS-LES calculation whose RANS layer is integrated to the wall, an embedded,
  two-scale or zonal near-wall solution coupled to a coarser outer calculation, and a
  two-layer or damped near-wall closure compared as a near-wall treatment are within
  the published rule when the source presents the method as a wall model,
  wall-modelled LES, wall function or near-wall treatment, or as a means of avoiding
  the wall-parallel resolution of a wall-resolved calculation. A contrast or design is
  marked `sublayer_resolving` when, in every calculation that carries it, the
  wall-normal grid reaches the viscous sublayer (first-cell height at or below about
  five wall units, or the source says the sublayer or near-wall region is resolved in
  the wall-normal direction). A work whose every coupled design is so marked is a
  **scope-boundary work**. Every count is reported with and without sublayer-resolving
  contrasts and scope-boundary works. A calculation that resolves the near-wall
  turbulence in all directions and tests no alternative treatment stays outside.
- **S2, estimators never coupled to a solver.** A relation that returns the wall shear
  stress from off-wall flow quantities, evaluated on reference data, is "a stress
  estimator" under the published rule whether or not the source calls it a wall model.
  A forecast of future wall stress is recorded as such (the published prescribed-input
  rule already separates it). A model whose output is not a wall quantity (a surrogate
  of a whole field; a model of a near-wall velocity signal) is not a stress estimator.
  An eligible work admitted only under S2, whose source never presents the estimator
  as a wall model or boundary condition, is also listed as a scope-boundary work.
- **S3, comparison by statement.** A design qualifies when values of the calculation
  and of a comparator appear in a table, a plot or the text. A comparison made only
  by a statement, with no displayed or quoted values, does not qualify a design. A
  work with no other qualifying design is recorded as contested.

The sublayer question (7) is put for every eligible work that has a hybrid RANS-LES
design or whose record in either reading contains one of the screening terms listed
in `codes/stage_settlement.py` (hybrid, detached-eddy, two-layer, enhanced wall
treatment, low-Reynolds-number model, integration to the wall, resolved sublayer,
two-scale, embedded, zonal, near-wall block). The screen reads the readers' records,
not the full texts: a sublayer-resolving method that neither reader described in
those terms would be missed. S2 is checked for every eligible work without a coupled
design. S3 can only be found by a reading made without the earlier disposition, so it
is checked for the 74 works read twice in this pass and remains unchecked for the 41
others.

## What the third reading does and what the script does

The third reader sees both readings and the source, quotes the passages and states
the facts the source supports, with an attribution for each disagreement. It is not
blind. The canonical record is then produced by `codes/build_v2.py` from the frozen
first reading and a list of operations (`settlement.json`), one per changed fact,
each with its quote, page and attribution. Memberships, labels and statuses are again
derived by `codes/facts.py`; none is typed. Where the third reading finds that the
rule does not decide a fact, the fact keeps the first-reading value, the item is
listed as a rule ambiguity, and for transfer rows the status is recorded as selection
unresolved, as the plan of 10:02 UTC prescribes.

## Decisions (unchanged from agreement_plan_v2.md)

- A tier that failed (a), (b) or (c) on the fresh sample is not quotable as a count,
  whatever the settlement finds. No sample top-up, no change of statistic.
- A tier or group that passed its statistical criteria becomes quotable when every
  listed disagreement has a quoted, attributed answer and the canonical data carry
  every correction. The quotable number is the settled count.
- `decisions_v2.json` records, for each tier and group, the statistics, the settled
  count, the count without scope-boundary items, the attribution of every
  disagreement and the reason for the decision.
